item.title: US Marine indicted in alleged Okinawa robbery homicide
item.description: A 20-year-old U.S. Marine stationed in Okinawa, Japan, has been indicted on charges murder and robbery.

item.title: Israelis have changed. Will they change their leadership?
item.description: Israel is holding a general election this week after years of war. For many Israelis, shaken by the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks and years of war, it is the most consequential in decades.

item.title: Moore: Key races in South 'in play,' Democrats 'made mistakes' not investing earlier
item.description: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore joined "This Week" Sunday for an interview about the midterm elections.

item.title: What makes a good spine-tingler? Stephen Graham Jones says it's all in the ending
item.description: Horror writer Stephen Graham Jones says horror's current moment is powered by more than just fear.

item.title: Live: French far-right leader Le Pen seeks to leverage unrest in presidential campaign kick-off
item.description: Marine Le Pen, leader of France’s far-right National Rally, is set to address some 10,000 supporters on Sunday in the city of Orleans as she kicks off her presidential campaign, a day after nationwide cost-of-living protests flared again into violence. Le Pen, the frontrunner, is seen to be benefiting in the polls from the weeks of unrest.

item.title: France: 110.000 protesters in Paris
item.description: Hundreds of demonstrations took place across France on Saturday over the rising cost of living, with security forces deployed in large numbers to prevent a repeat of the violence seen last weekend. While the marches themselves “passed off well” in several cities, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said members of “ultra-left” groups threw projectiles and fireworks at police in an attempt to provoke clashes. French Communist Party spokesperson Fatima Khallouk shares more details.

item.title: Calais, 10 years after the Jungle: Migrants still risk the Channel crossing
item.description: Ten years ago, in 2016, thousands of #migrants lived in what was known as the “Great #Jungle”, a vast camp on the outskirts of #Calais. It took the authorities seven days to dismantle it. Today, dozens of smaller “jungles” are scattered across a wider stretch of the coastline. These camps are dismantled every 48 hours on average. For migrants, the goal remains the same: to cross the Channel and reach the United Kingdom. Despite the risks posed by “small boats”, these makeshift vessels, many continue to attempt the crossing in the hope of a better life. Our reporters Pauline Godart, Claire Paccalin and Mohamed Farhat travelled to northern France for #BilletRetour.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom aims for deep-red Mississippi Senate seat
item.description: In a climate where polls show Trump's approval cratering, Dems are optimistic about Scott Colom's chances of flipping Republican senator's seat in deep-red Mississippi.

item.title: Struggling London-listed media group Future rebuffs interest in The Week
item.description: The struggling London-listed company which owns Go Compare, the price comparison platform, has rebuffed indicative bid interest in The Week, the current affairs magazine.

item.title: Presidential runoff under way in Brazil
item.description: Brazil is also heading to the polls today for a run-off vote that will decide who leads the country. The race is on a knife edge between incumbent left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio scored a major upset in the first round earlier this month, taking the lead in the vote. The campaign has been dominated by corruption scandals, economic difficulties and allegations of US interference, which Washington has denied. France 24 correspondent Jan Onoszko reports the latest from Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Le Pen leads polls with up to 38% six months before election
item.description: The day after the first day of the National Rally congress in Orléans, in central France, passed without any major incidents, Marine Le Pen is due to deliver her first major campaign speech on Sunday afternoon, 25 October, under heavy police surveillance. The speech, centred on the theme of renewal, aims to inject a dose of optimism six months ahead of the presidential election, the candidate has reportedly said in private. Gilles Ivaldi, a political science researcher at the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) and the University of Nice, explains that the violence following protests across France in recent weeks could help the National Rally present itself as the party capable of restoring public safety and national security.

item.title: France: Le Pen launches presidential campaign in Orleans
item.description: Far-right leader Marine Le Pen is launching her presidential campaign today. The National Rally candidate is due to deliver her first campaign speech in Orléans, addressing around 10,000 party members. Police were controlling traffic entering the city this morning, following a large anti-far-right demonstration on Saturday, where thousands of protesters marched chanting anti-fascist slogans.

item.title: 12 injured, including 6 children, in shooting near Florida university, police say
item.description: At least 11 of those injured had gunshot wounds, police said.

item.title: The week in pictures: Protests across France, wildfires in Indonesia and Brazilian elections
item.description: From student protests across France over the weekend and presidential elections in Brazil pitting leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro to wildfires in Indonesia, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

item.title: Voting under way across Brazil in tight presidential run-off between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro
item.description: Brazil’s 158 million voters decide between leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Senator Flavio Bolsonaro – the son of former president and Trump ally Jair Bolsonaro – following a highly charged run-off campaign period, with the candidates in a dead heat in polls. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Polls open in Brazil presidential runoff
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and sight-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro faced off Friday in their second and final debate ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff election. The two candidates repeated their campaign proposals, focusing on the cost of living and security, while exchanging ⁠allegations of corruption. France 24 Jan Onoszko telles us the latest from Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Far-right leader Le Pen says visible policing keeps protests smooth
item.description: Meanwhile, France’s far-right National Rally is holding the second day of its party congress in Orléans, south of Paris. Marine Le Pen is expected to officially launch her presidential campaign in a speech later this afternoon, while Jordan Bardella is being re-elected as party leader. On Saturday, a large counter-demonstration against the far right was held in the city. Our reporter Antonia Kerrigan has been following the latest developments.

item.title: Israel: Demonstrators rally against government ahead of election
item.description: In Israel, the anti-Netanyahu movement is mobilising. Thousands gathered in Tel Aviv on Friday to protest against the Israeli government, just three days ahead of a general election widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

item.title: Obama hits campaign trail for democrats
item.description: With less than two weeks to go before the US midterm elections, former President Barack Obama has hit the campaign trail, rallying support for Democratic candidates in the key states of Michigan and Ohio. He criticised the Trump administration, blaming the White House for rising living costs, a major concern for voters. Democrats are hoping to regain control of Congress, with polls showing several closely contested races. Ophelie Jacobson has more.

item.title: West Bank: Families forcibly displaced in Hebron
item.description: More Palestinian families have been displaced in the occupied West Bank as Israeli forces continue operations in Hebron, following a deadly shooting that killed two Israeli soldiers on Friday. With elections scheduled for Tuesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed a heavy response to the attack. Morgaene Ayre has the latest.

item.title: The College of Magic turns ordinary kids into confident, top-hat wearing magicians
item.description: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.

item.title: At least 1,300 people arrested in mass weekend protests across France
item.description: At least 1,300 people were arrested on the sidelines of Saturday's protests across France and at least 50 officers and three protesters were hurt, the interior ministry said Sunday. The arrests occurred as clashes broke out on the margins of largely calm demonstrations in major cities over the high cost of living.

item.title: Suspect in racist Paris shooting transferred to psychiatric unit, had drugs in his system
item.description: A shooter suspected of killing one person and wounding five others on Friday in the town of Trappes, near Paris, has had his police custody suspended for a 48-hour psychiatric observation, anti-terror prosecutors said Sunday. The 39-year-old man is believed to have had racist motivations behind the gun attack as most of the victims had foreign origins.

item.title: When a teen posts a selfie, how much filter is 'too much' filter?
item.description: The recent Meta settlement includes a clause banning "cosmetic procedure filters" for teens. But defining what constitutes an extreme makeover isn't easy.

item.title: Bus and lorry collide killing 22, including passengers returning from funeral
item.description: At least 22 people have been killed after a bus and lorry collided in Kenya, police say.

item.title: France: Some clashes erupted at end of protests
item.description: There were some clashes on Saturday, mainly in major cities and as demonstrations came to an end. French authorities say police made nearly 1,000 arrests nationwide. Here’s a report from our sister channel, France 2.

item.title: More than 400.000 protest across France
item.description: Saturday’s demonstrations across France were largely peaceful, easing fears of a repeat of the violence seen last weekend. Hundreds of thousands took to the streets to demand action on the rising cost of living and more funding for public services, with students, workers and retirees marching side by side. Many say their anger shows no sign of fading. The government put turnout at 410,000 nationwide, while the CGT union estimated the figure was almost twice as high. Here’s Jack Pownall with more.

item.title: France’s far right gathers as Le Pen prepares her presidential campaign
item.description: Meanwhile, France’s far-right National Rally is holding the second day of its party congress in Orléans, south of Paris. Marine Le Pen is expected to officially launch her presidential campaign in a speech later this afternoon, while Jordan Bardella is being re-elected as party leader. On Saturday, a large counter-demonstration against the far right was held in the city. For more on what’s happening there, let’s cross to our reporter, Antonia Kerrigan.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march in France to protest against government
item.description: Hundreds of thousands marched across France on Saturday protesting the rising cost of living and a lack of government resources for essential services like schools. While demonstrations in Paris started peacefully they ended with a heavy security response, with almost 1,000 arrested across the country. France 24 International Affairs Editor Oliver Farry shares further details.

item.title: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are
item.description: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.

item.title: Independent candidates sense a moment. Some Democrats hope they're right.
item.description: As they look to win the Senate, Democrats are hoping that independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana can help them topple Republicans in a part of the country where their own brand is hurting.

item.title: In Arkansas, Democrats see an opening at the edge of the competitive midterms map
item.description: In a sign of the potentially dire midterm political environment, Republicans have spent millions of dollars playing defense in Arkansas, one of the most conservative states in the country.

item.title: Student protesters aim for electoral victory over Serbia's long-serving leader
item.description: People in Serbia are voting in a parliamentary election that is being viewed as a showdown between former president Aleksandar Vucic and a university student protest movement.

item.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe
item.description: While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.

item.title: Serbia holds parliamentary election as populist leader Vucic faces student movement
item.description: Serbia votes on Sunday in what is set to be its most contested parliamentary election in more than 14 years, as a student-led movement seeks to oust the party of populist leader Aleksandar Vucic. The vote comes after nearly two years of student-led protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a canopy that killed 16 people.

item.title: What to know as Brazilians choose between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro in tense presidential runoff
item.description: Brazilians are set on Sunday to choose between leftist incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro in the runoff vote of a deeply polarizing presidential election, and one which will determine whether the US significantly expands its growing influence in Latin America.

item.title: Drought, fire and high diesel prices 'addin' up tough' for Oregon ranchers
item.description: Record diesel prices are kicking Western ranchers while they're down. Drought means they have to buy extra hay, and pay truckers extra to deliver it because of fuel price hikes.

item.description: Brazilians are going to the polls today to elect a president in a run-off vote that is being closely watched around the world.
